claims.text: Metabolic syndrome affected 68.0% of breast cancer survivors receiving adjuvant endocrine therapy.
Overall prevalence of metabolic syndrome did not differ significantly between aromatase inhibitor users (72.7%) and tamoxifen users (63.0%, p = 0.202).
Aromatase inhibitor users had lower HDL-cholesterol compared to tamoxifen users.
Aromatase inhibitor users had higher fasting glucose compared to tamoxifen users.
Aromatase inhibitor users had higher blood pressure compared to tamoxifen users.
Tamoxifen users had higher triglycerides compared to aromatase inhibitor users.
Higher physical activity level was independently associated with lower odds of metabolic syndrome (OR = 0.44 per 0.1-unit increase; 95% CI: 0.28–0.68; p < 0.001).
Greater Mediterranean diet adherence was independently associated with lower odds of metabolic syndrome (OR = 0.72; 95% CI: 0.60–0.87; p = 0.001).
The multivariable prediction model for metabolic syndrome showed an apparent AUC of 0.832 and a 5-fold cross-validated AUC of 0.800.
The multivariable prediction model for metabolic syndrome had a Hosmer–Lemeshow calibration p-value of 0.400.

methodologies.name: Cross-sectional multivariable logistic regression analysis
methodologies.description: Cross-sectional study assessing metabolic syndrome (IDF 2006 criteria) and its associations with Mediterranean diet adherence (culturally adapted 14-item MEDAS) and physical activity levels (GENI software) in breast cancer survivors.
datasets: 150 women receiving adjuvant endocrine therapy in Oran, Algeria (May 2022–December 2025)

limitations.text: Given the cross-sectional design, these associations cannot establish causality.

future_work.text: Further prospective and interventional research to determine whether modifying Mediterranean diet adherence and physical activity could reduce metabolic syndrome risk.
